clues: This city in north Kazakhstan stretches along the south shore of a lake. It lies at the south edge of wide dry grass plains.
Winters here are long, deep cold, and snowy, lasting more than five months. Summers flip the tale, with warm, dry, sunny days.
This city began in 1824 as a small army fort. It did not gain full city rank until much later, in 1895.
This town is a cross point for two great rail lines. One runs through its land, and one serves the south of Siberia.
In the end, this town is the capital of its wide region in the north of the land.
